test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 16 Jun, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: AB is a chord in the minor segment of a circle of centre Q. P is a point on the major arc AB. The tangents drawn from external point D to the circle are AD and BD. If ∠APB = 39°, then find the measure of ∠ADB.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The angle subtended by a chord at the **center** is twice the angle subtended at the **major arc**: ∠AQB = 2 × ∠APB.

In a circle, the angle between two **tangents** from an external point and the angle subtended by the chord of contact at the center are **supplementary**.

⇒ ∠ADB = 180° − ∠AQB

⇒ ∠ADB = 180° − (2 × 39°) = 180° − 78° = 102°.

**∴ The correct answer is 102°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** ∠APB = 39°, **Q** is the center, **AD** and **BD** are tangents from external point **D**.

**Formula Used:** ∠Center = 2 × ∠Circumference; Sum of angles in quadrilateral = 360°.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ccc9f8d9398efa0d97b79c415df95d30a1885e3ab396c00506a6025fd6293a7f.png] 

⇒ The angle subtended by chord **AB** at the center **Q** is twice the angle at point **P** on the major arc.

⇒ ∠AQB = 2 × ∠APB = 2 × 39° = 78°

⇒ In quadrilateral **AQBD**, the radii **QA** and **QB** are perpendicular to tangents **AD** and **BD** respectively.

⇒ ∠QAD = 90° and ∠QBD = 90°

⇒ Sum of angles in **AQBD** = 360°

⇒ ∠AQB + ∠QAD + ∠QBD + ∠ADB = 360°

⇒ 78° + 90° + 90° + ∠ADB = 360°

⇒ 258° + ∠ADB = 360°

⇒ ∠ADB = 360° − 258° = 102°

**∴ The correct answer is 102°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Angle at Center Theorem

The angle subtended by an arc at the center of a circle is double the angle subtended by it at any point on the remaining part of the circle.

Tangent-Radius Property

A tangent at any point of a circle is perpendicular to the radius through the point of contact (∠Radius, Tangent = 90°).

Tangent Quadrilateral

In a quadrilateral formed by two radii and two tangents from an external point, the opposite angles at the center and the external point are supplementary (sum = 180°).</p
